Colombia has a defined procedure for authorizing living modified organisms (LMOs) for exclusively agricultural, livestock, fisheries, commercial forest plantation and agro-industrial purposes. The Colombian Agricultural Institute (ICA) runs it under Resolution 91505 of 2021, which implements Decree 4525 of 2005 and Law 740 of 2002, the law by which Colombia ratified the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety.

The flowchart below follows an application from filing to the ICA decision. Select any step to read what happens, who is involved and which article of the Resolution applies.

The process in brief

  1. Application. The interested party files a signed request with the ICA through the information system the institute provides.
  2. Requirements check. The ICA reviews the application within 10 business days of filing. If it is complete, it moves straight to public consultation. If not, the ICA asks once for clarification or additional documents, and the applicant has up to 15 business days to respond. Without a response, the application is treated as withdrawn.
  3. Public consultation and risk assessment. The application is open to public consultation for 15 calendar days. At the same time, the ICA evaluates the potential risks of the proposed activity, case by case, and prepares a report for the National Technical Biosafety Committee (CTNBio).
  4. CTNBio review. The ICA convenes the CTNBio within 15 calendar days after the consultation ends. The committee examines the report and the measures to avoid, prevent, mitigate, correct or compensate possible risks, and may ask the applicant for more information (15 business days to respond).
  5. CTNBio recommendation. The committee recommends to approve, not to approve, or to carry out biosafety tests. When tests are required, the applicant runs the field phase and the ICA monitors it. The ICA presents the results report to the CTNBio within 30 business days after the test ends, and the committee then recommends whether or not to approve the event.
  6. ICA decision. After analyzing the recommendation, the ICA authorizes or denies the requested activities through a reasoned resolution, issued within 10 business days after the CTNBio meeting. Authorized uses in the flowchart are feed, cultivation and research (contained use).

Deadlines set in the Resolution

Public consultation15 calendar days

Legal basis

  • Law 740 of 2002, which approves the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety
  • Decree 4525 of 2005, which regulates Law 740 of 2002
  • ICA Resolution 91505 of 2021, which sets the procedure for LMO applications
  • ICA Resolution 91506 of 2021, which governs the CTNBio

This page is an explanatory summary. The official text of the Resolution prevails.
